meta.slice: S15 — THE EASTERN SYSTEMATIZERS, COMPILERS AND POPULARIZERS. The functional counterparts of Manly P. Hall (syncretic encyclopedist), Crowley (systematizer who founds a current and writes prolifically) and Stephen Skinner (scholar-practitioner who edits and republishes operative texts with apparatus), for the Indian/Indic operative corpus. Figures: Sir John Woodroffe / 'Arthur Avalon' and his Indian collaborators; Ram Kumar Rai and Prachya Prakashan; Mike Magee (Prachya's OTHER English translator — a correction to the brief); Panchanan Tarkaratna and the Bengali Sanskrit-editor trade; Gopinath Kaviraj; Swami Sivananda; Swami Satyananda Saraswati and the Bihar School; Alain Daniélou; Monier Monier-Williams and H. H. Wilson; Jaideva Singh; Mark Dyczkowski; Swami Lakshmanjoo (and Paul Reps as the hinge); B. V. Raman; David Frawley / Vamadeva Shastri; Osho / Rajneesh. NOT in scope and deliberately excluded: the primary Sanskrit corpus itself (S10 owns it) and the academic criticism literature (a third agent owns it). This slice records the MEDIATION LAYER — who put the operative corpus into English, on what evidence, with what apparatus, and under what licence.
meta.method: WebSearch/WebFetch on library catalogues (Wellcome Collection), publisher catalogues (Exotic India, Prachya Prakashan listing), Wikipedia (used as a *pointer* to dated bibliography, never as the evidentiary ground for a contested claim), Banglapedia, the Australian Royal Commission's own case-study page, Open Library, and the Sannyas Wiki's per-book bibliographic records. meta.operativeContentRazor: THIS FILE SHIPS NO QUOTED OPERATIVE TEXT (FRAMING §10 blockers gate the first quotation). It records THAT a text or a modern manual sets out a procedure — its type, structure, completeness, harm profile and citation. No mantra syllables, no yantra templates, no quantities, no timings, no second-person instruction, no ṣaṭkarma finger-assignments, no prāṇāyāma ratios. Where a source I read DOES contain such material (Ullrey n.45 quotes Rai's Ḍāmara rendering of the six-acts finger assignments verbatim) the fact is recorded and the content is not.
meta.pdDoctrine: Per-EDITION, US determination, per FRAMING §4.1-§4.3. The 1930-or-earlier threshold is the operative one for this round (works published 1930 or earlier entered the US public domain 1 Jan 2026; 1931 follows 1 Jan 2027). Consequence that BITES this slice specifically: the Tantrik Texts series straddles the line — vols I-XV (1913-1929) are PD-US, vol XVI Kaulāvalīnirṇaya (1928) is PD-US, vol XIII Mahānirvāṇa (1929) is PD-US, but vols 16-22 (1933-1944) are NOT, and neither is anything by Rai, Dyczkowski, Jaideva Singh, Satyananda, Daniélou, Frawley or Osho. The single most important modern English gateway into the operative tantras — Prachya Prakashan's Tantra Granthamālā — is entirely CITE-ONLY.
meta.livingPeopleNote: Frawley (b. 1950) is living and politically active; the Satyananda/Bihar School institutions and the Osho movement are live and litigious; the Royal Commission material concerns identified survivors. Every contested row here carries every position, names who holds it, and adjudicates nothing. Where a Commission declined to make a finding, this file says the Commission declined to make a finding — it does not convert untested evidence into a fact, and it does not suppress that the evidence was given.

authors.name: Sir John George Woodroffe
authors.role: Barrister; Advocate then Judge (1904) then Chief Justice (1915) of the Calcutta High Court; Tagore Law Professor; later Reader in Indian Law, Oxford. The Skinner analogue: a scholar-practitioner who commissioned, edited and republished operative texts with apparatus, in a numbered series, for a Western readership.

authors.name: Atal Bihari Ghosh (A. B. Ghose)
authors.role: Woodroffe's chief collaborator and, on Taylor's account, the principal source of the Sanskrit textual knowledge that appears under the Avalon name. Named nowhere in the books themselves.

authors.name: Tārānātha Vidyāratna
authors.role: Sanskrit editor of Tantrik Texts vols I, II, III and V — i.e. the person who actually constituted the Sanskrit text of the Kulārṇava and Prapañcasāra editions the anglophone world has used ever since.

authors.name: The other Tantrik Texts editors
authors.role: Girīśa Chandra Vedāntatīrtha (IV), Pārvatī Charaṇa Tarkatīrtha (VI), Kazi Dawa Samdup (VII, the Buddhist volume), Lakṣmaṇa Śāstrī (VIII), Svāmī Vimalānanda (IX), Naṭanānandanātha (X), Sītārāma Śāstrī (XI), Hariharānanda Bhāratī (XIII), Svāmī Trivikrama Tīrtha (XX), Pañcānana Bhaṭṭācārya (I later ed., XXI), Pañcānana Śāstrī (XXII).

authors.name: Ram Kumar Rai (Rāmakumāra Rāya)
authors.dates: UNVERIFIED — no birth or death year located this round
authors.role: Varanasi translator-editor; the productive centre of Prachya Prakashan's Tantra Granthamālā. The single largest body of English renderings of Sanskrit mantraśāstra and operative tantra outside the academy.

authors.name: Michael (Mike) Magee
authors.role: Prachya Prakashan's OTHER English translator — Vāmakeśvarīmatam (TG 11) and Kaulajñāna-nirṇaya (TG 12), both 1986, both first English editions. The brief for this slice assumed Rai did all of the Prachya English work; he did not.

authors.name: Panchanan Tarkaratna
authors.role: Bhatpara-trained pandit; joined Bangabasi Press 1886; the industrial Bengali Sanskrit-editor-translator, who put the Purāṇas, Smṛtis and epics into printed Sanskrit-with-Bengali form for a mass market.

authors.name: Mahāmahopādhyāya Gopinath Kaviraj
authors.role: The great scholar-insider of Banaras: librarian of the Sarasvatī Bhavana (1914-1920), Principal of the Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (1923-1937), editor of the Sarasvatī Bhavana Granthamālā through which he published 72 Sanskrit works; head of the Yoga-Tantra department at Varanaseya Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya from 1964.

authors.name: Swami Sivananda Saraswati
authors.role: Physician turned renunciate; founded the Divine Life Society (1936) and the Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy; the prolific COMPILER — the output is variously counted at 200+, 296 and 300+ titles, which is itself a datum about how compilation-scale work resists enumeration.

authors.name: Swami Satyananda Saraswati
authors.role: Sivananda's disciple; founded the International Yoga Fellowship (1962) and the Bihar School of Yoga (Munger, 1964). The SYSTEMATIZER: he converted a scattered operative corpus into a graded, examinable modern curriculum with a house press.

authors.name: Alain Daniélou
authors.role: French musicologist and Indologist; Banaras Hindu University 1935-1953; initiated under Swami Karpatri as Shiva Sharan. The Western insider-systematizer — he writes from inside a Śaiva initiatory frame and against academic Indology, and is contested for exactly that.

authors.name: Sir Monier Monier-Williams
authors.role: Boden Professor of Sanskrit, Oxford, from 1860. Lexicographer and framer: the dictionary is the tool everyone after him uses, and the framing essays are the lens.

authors.name: Horace Hayman Wilson
authors.role: First Boden Professor of Sanskrit (elected 1832); Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Bengal. His 'Sketch of the Religious Sects of the Hindus' is the taxonomy that fixed the English-language category grid for Indian sectarian religion, including the tantric sects.

authors.name: Jaideva Singh
authors.role: Musicologist and philosopher (Padma Bhushan 1974); studied the Kashmiri Śaiva texts word by word with Swami Lakshman Joo and published the results as Sanskrit-with-English editions through Motilal Banarsidass. The transmission channel by which Trika reached English readers.

authors.name: Mark S. G. Dyczkowski
authors.role: Oxford DPhil under Alexis Sanderson and Richard Gombrich; initiated by Swami Lakshman Joo (1976); resident in Varanasi. Both an academic Indologist and an initiate — the purest scholar-practitioner in the set, and the producer of the largest single critical-and-translated operative corpus in the field.

authors.name: Swami Lakshmanjoo (Lakshman Joo Raina)
authors.role: The last widely-acknowledged holder of the Kashmiri Trika oral lineage. He wrote comparatively little; his corpus exists because Westerners recorded him. The Crowley-inverse: a systematizer whose system was published BY his students, not by him.

authors.name: Paul Reps
authors.role: Not an Indologist and not in the brief — included because he is the documented hinge. His 'Centering' is the rendering through which the Vijñāna Bhairava reached the Western counterculture, and Osho's use of it is acknowledged in print.

authors.name: Bangalore Venkata Raman
authors.role: Editor of The Astrological Magazine for 62+ years from 1936 (the magazine was his grandfather B. Suryanarain Rao's before him). The astrological systematizer-populariser: he standardised what anglophone readers mean by 'Hindu astrology'.

authors.name: David Frawley / Pandit Vamadeva Shastri
authors.role: American writer; founder of the American Institute of Vedic Studies. The modern Western-Vedic systematizer: he packaged jyotiṣa, āyurveda and Vedic studies into a single teachable 'Vedic science', and is simultaneously a Hindutva-aligned political writer. Contested on both counts.

authors.name: Osho / Bhagwan Shree Rajneesh (Chandra Mohan Jain)
authors.role: The sharpest Crowley analogue in the set: a prolific charismatic systematizer who founded a current, commented on a primary operative text at enormous length, and left a legacy contested to the point of criminality.

authors.name: Kathleen Taylor
authors.role: Historian (SOAS); author of the 2001 authorship study that reframes every Woodroffe row in this graph. NOT a systematizer — carried as an author node because her monograph is filed as a work.

authors.name: C. G. Jung
authors.role: OUT-OF-SLICE node, carried only as the target of one NOT-ASSERTED reception edge (the 1932 Kundalini seminar and the annotated Serpent Power in his library). Another slice owns him.

authors.name: Alexis Sanderson
authors.role: OUT-OF-SLICE node (S10 owns him as a source). Carried because he supervised Dyczkowski at Oxford — the one documented teaching edge linking this slice's scholar-practitioner wing to the academic Śaiva-literature spine.

authors.name: Michael Ullrey

works.author: au:woodroffe
works.dateText: 1913 (English translation and introduction); Sanskrit text as Tantrik Texts XIII, 1929, ed. Hariharānanda Bhāratī

editions.translator: Arthur Avalon (John Woodroffe), with the collaboration Taylor attributes to A. B. Ghose

contested.question: How much of the translation is Woodroffe's?

positions.claim: Published under 'Arthur Avalon' 'to denote that they had been written with the direct cooperation of others and in particular with the assistance of one of my friends who will not permit me to mention his name.'
The unnamed friend and chief collaborator was Atal Bihari Ghose, who was the chief source of the textual knowledge; Woodroffe also made extensive use of secondary sources.

contested.resolution: Both positions are the SAME position seen from two sides — Woodroffe said in print that he was not working alone; Taylor identified who. What remains genuinely open, and is not resolved here, is the per-volume division of labour.

works.title: The Serpent Power
works.titleOriginal: Ṣaṭcakranirūpaṇa (of Pūrṇānanda) + Pādukāpañcaka, translated with an introduction
works.author: au:woodroffe
works.dateText: 1918 (Wikipedia's bibliography gives 1919; 1918 is the date usually printed). Sanskrit text = Tantrik Texts II, 1913.

editions.publisher: Ganesh & Co., Madras / Luzac & Co., London

editions.pdStatus: reprint of PD text; the reprint's own new matter is not PD

procedures.typeAsFiled: kuṇḍalinī-yoga: an ordered ascent through six cakras with per-cakra visualisation content
procedures.completenessBasis: The Ṣaṭcakranirūpaṇa is a DESCRIPTIVE anatomy of the subtle body — it enumerates cakras, petals, seed-syllables, presiding deities and the ascent — and it is not a stepwise operating manual: the breath work, posture and duration that would make it executable are not in it. Woodroffe's long introduction supplies context, not method. Grade 'partial' is therefore about the SOURCE TEXT, not about the translation.
procedures.evidence: The text's structure is uncontroversial and is described in every account of it; no page-level citation was taken this round. FLAGGED for audit.
procedures.harmNote: Downstream, not internal. This book is the proximate ancestor of Western kuṇḍalinī practice, a domain with documented adverse-experience literature; and the modern practices attached to it routinely involve breath retention, which engages FRAMING C-3. Nothing here reproduces a ratio or a technique.

contested.question: Is the modern Western chakra system Indian or a modern Western construction built on this book?

positions.claim: The Western chakra system is a modern composite — Theosophical clairvoyants, Indologists, Jung, Campbell, Esalen — that reached its familiar seven-quality form around 1977; Jung and Campbell were working from Woodroffe's Serpent Power.
The seven-chakra colour-and-quality system is ancient Indian doctrine.

contested.resolution: Not adjudicated. Leland's is a published historical argument and is reported as his; the popular position is reported as the popular position. Leland's book was NOT read this round.

contested.question: Is Woodroffe's presentation faithful or a reframing?

positions.claim: Woodroffe's work is a Victorian-modernist apologetic — it defends tantra against colonial and missionary contempt by rendering it philosophically respectable, and this shapes what is emphasised and what is muted.

Whatever the Western framing, the reception is Indian too: 'most Indians declare the greatest scholar of tantra to be Arthur Avalon', and South Asian interpretations of tantra 'are valid developments in the tantra tradition' rather than corruptions of it.

contested.resolution: Not adjudicated. The two are not straightforwardly opposed — Taylor is about production, Ullrey about reception — and this file records both without merging them.

contested.question: How should the Bihar School corpus be handled given the abuse findings?

positions.holder: Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, Case Study 21 (report 2016)
positions.claim: Swami Akhandananda Saraswati — who oversaw the Mangrove Mountain ashram from about 1974 — sexually abused children there; he was convicted in 1989 and sentenced to two years four months. The Commission was satisfied that 'the Satyananda yoga doctrine in Australia at the time, and as interpreted by Akhandananda together with the particular belief system and culture at the Mangrove ashram, created significant barriers to the capacity of child victims … to disclose'.

positions.holder: Two witnesses at the same public hearing
positions.claim: They were abused by Satyananda himself.
It was treated as outside the scope of the case study and was untested; NO FINDING was made against Satyananda.

positions.claim: Continue to publish and teach the corpus.

contested.resolution: NOT ADJUDICATED, and deliberately. The distinction the record actually supports is stated exactly: a conviction and adverse findings as to Akhandananda and as to the institution; evidence given but untested and no finding as to Satyananda. Suppressing the second would misrepresent the hearing; asserting it would misrepresent the report. FLAG: the report PDF itself was not read this round.

contested.question: Is Daniélou an insider reporting the tradition or a systematizer imposing a thesis?

positions.holder: Critics as summarised by the Fondation Alain Daniélou itself (Transcultural Dialogues n°2/n°5)
positions.claim: His extension of Śaivism beyond India and 'programmatic amalgamation of it with Dionysian religion' is 'an abuse in the field of comparative religion'; his Aryan-invader vs Dravidian-autochthon framing is 'unacceptable speculation in light of contemporary archaeological research'; and his comparatism takes elements out of context and over-interprets them.
The criticisms miss the point because the scope and consequences of his readings differ from what detractors assume; his interpretation of Śaivism has problems but not the ones charged.
He writes from inside an initiated Śaiva frame (initiated under Swami Karpatri as Shiva Sharan) and against academic Indology's authority to adjudicate.

contested.resolution: NOT ADJUDICATED. AUDIT TARGET: the only summary of the critique located this round is published by the subject's own foundation. A slice that reported 'Daniélou is criticised for X' on the strength of his defenders' characterisation of X would be laundering. The charge is recorded WITH that provenance attached.

structuralFindings: THE PUBLIC-DOMAIN INVERSION, stated precisely for this slice. Everything quotable is Orientalist framing (Wilson 1828-1840, Monier-Williams 1872/1891/1899) or Woodroffe's pre-1930 volumes. Everything that would let a reader check an operative claim against a modern, competent rendering — Rai, Magee, Jaideva Singh, Dyczkowski, Lakshmanjoo, Satyananda, Daniélou, Frawley, Osho — is CITE-ONLY without exception. FRAMING §4.4 predicts that the PD constraint selects the worst witnesses; in this slice it selects them with a completeness of about 100%.

THE SANSKRIT-VS-ENGLISH GATE IS THE REAL PD BOUNDARY. Woodroffe's Tantrik Texts are quotable, but most volumes are Sanskrit-only, so 'quotable' confers no capability on an English reader. The English gateway is entirely modern and entirely closed. That is the single most important fact for anyone planning what this repo can actually show.

THE MEDIATION LAYER IS WHERE THE OPERATIVE CONTENT IS ACTUALLY OPERABLE. The Sanskrit tantras are, on this graph's own grades, overwhelmingly 'referenced' or 'partial' — they presume a teacher. The MODERN works are the ones graded 'complete': APMB (1969), Kundalini Tantra (1984), Yoga Nidra (1976), Hindu Predictive Astrology (1938), Astrology of the Seers (1990), The Yoga of Herbs (1986), Reps's Centering (1957). The systematizers did not merely transmit an operative corpus; they COMPLETED it, and the completion is theirs.

TWO DISTINCT FAITHFULNESS FAILURES, and conflating them is the standard error. (a) SELECTION failure: Woodroffe made the late, reformist Mahānirvāṇa the flagship, so the most-read tantra in English is atypical of its corpus. (b) CONSTRUCTION failure: Satyananda's yoga nidrā and Frawley's 'Vedic astrology' are modern builds carrying ancient labels. Neither is a mistranslation. A slice that only asked 'is the rendering accurate' would find nothing wrong with either.

THE COMPLETENESS AXIS IS LEVEL-RELATIVE, and the Vijñānabhairava proves it. The set of 112 dhāraṇās is COMPLETE in Singh, in Reps and in Osho; every individual dhāraṇā is REFERENCED in all three, because each is a one-line pointer. Any grading scheme that assigns one completeness value per work will get this text wrong in both directions.

PRACHYA PRAKASHAN IS A TWO-TRANSLATOR HOUSE, NOT ONE. Rai carries the mantraśāstra and Ḍāmara/Kaula bulk; Magee carries the Śrīvidyā (TG 11) and the Kaulajñānanirṇaya (TG 12), both 1986, both first English editions. The brief's assumption that Rai did all of it would have mis-attributed two firsts.

THE ONE REAL TRANSMISSION CHAIN IN THIS SLICE IS THREE NODES LONG AND FULLY DOCUMENTED: Lakshman Joo (oral, Kashmir, 1950s) → Reps, 'Centering' (1957) → Osho, The Book of the Secrets (1972-74; acknowledgment printed 1977). It survives the ASSERTED test at every link because every link has a printed artefact — a permissions line, not a resemblance. Everything else in this slice that looks like transmission is either institutional succession or an untested assumption, and is filed as such.

THE HONOURED INDIAN SCHOLARSHIP IS NOT IN ENGLISH. Kaviraj's Sahitya Akademi-winning tantra study (1964) is in Hindi with no English edition; Tarkaratna's corpus is Bengali; Rai's Mantra Mahārṇava is Hindi. The anglophone default authorities on tantra are a British judge writing in 1913-1922 and a Varanasi publisher's English list from the 1980s. That asymmetry is not incidental to the field's shape — it IS the field's shape.

THE HARM AXIS SPLITS CLEANLY BY MODE, and not by content. The TEXT-harm cases are ṣaṭkarma material (Rai's Mantramahodadhi and Ḍāmara; the Mahānirvāṇa's Kaula sections) and breath retention (Reps, Osho, Sivananda, Satyananda, the Vijñānabhairava line) — both are Route A under FRAMING §5.0, with a scarcity term near zero. The INSTITUTIONAL-harm cases are Rajneeshpuram (751 poisoned, a conviction) and the Satyananda Yoga Ashram Royal Commission findings — neither of which is a property of any text, and both of which are far better documented than any textual harm in the slice.

COMPLETENESS OF THE SET, NOT COMPLETENESS OF THE FIGURE, is what this slice could not achieve for four people. Ram Kumar Rai has no located birth or death year; Michael Magee has no verified dates; the Tantrik Texts volume-by-volume PD boundary rests on one non-academic aggregation; and the Royal Commission report itself was not read. Those four are the file's load-bearing weaknesses and are listed again in the notes.
